summary: Father Andrew discusses the accusation that Orthodox Christians practice idolatry by venerating icons, referencing the Seventh Ecumenical Council held in Nicaea in 787. He explains that the council declared depicting Christ is necessary because God became incarnate in Jesus Christ, meaning veneration directed at an icon is actually given to the person depicted. The discussion concludes that honoring material objects like icons or the Eucharist is consistent with Christian belief since God took on matter.
